reversal: Baylor is older than the state of Texas. It was chartered by the Republic of Texas, a sovereign country that ceased to exist eleven months later. Fifteen colleges got that charter. Baylor is the only one still operating under it.

beats.narration: This university is older than the state it stands in.
It was chartered by a country that no longer exists.
In eighteen forty-five, Texas was not yet American.
It was its own republic. Nine years old, deep in debt, and running out of time.
That winter, a petition for a Baptist university reached its congress.
Behind it, three men. A frontier judge, Robert Emmett Bledsoe Baylor. A missionary, James Huckins. And a pastor, William Milton Tryon.
The school was almost called San Jacinto. Then Milam.
Only just before the final vote did the petitioners ask that it carry the judge's name.
On the first of February, President Anson Jones signed it into law.
Eleven months later the republic was gone, annexed into the United States.
It had chartered fifteen colleges. Fourteen closed, merged, or vanished.
One still operates under the charter it was given. Older than Texas itself.
